title: GCP handoff releases node before protected response is committed
description: Security review finding: GatewayCoordinator::handle_post_handoff calls NodeRegistry::handle_handoff_request, which clones the node security/routing state and immediately unregisters the node. Gateway::dispatch_runtime_gcp only afterward reserves OSCORE sender state, encrypts, routes, and transmits the response; any sender-state persistence, encryption, route, or radio failure is merely logged while the node remains deleted. Thus an authenticated request can irreversibly discard ownership and OSCORE state without the requester receiving it. Make handoff transactional: stage/lease state, send a protected response, and commit release only after authenticated delivery/acknowledgement (or durably retain a retryable transfer record); rollback on every failure. Add failures at persistence, no-route, and transmit boundaries.
